maya: Quick bring-up for candidate 'lumenix-int6' on embeddings. Ran recall@10/100, cluster compactness and short-query stress on stack_holdout_8k.

reina: headline numbers?

maya: Baseline (lumen-v1) recall@10 = 0.814. lumenix-int6 recall@10 = 0.792 (delta -0.022). recall@100 delta smaller (-0.009). Paired bootstrap p=0.011.

tom: Which query slices?

maya: Biggest drops for short queries (<=3 tokens) and code snippets containing symbols (e.g., "map::insert"). Also punctuation-stripped variants hurt less.

reina: Any embedding norm shifts?

maya: Yes 5% lower mean norm; intra-cluster cosine fell 0.70 -> 0.66. Silhouette k=80: 0.34 -> 0.29.

tom: Did you try simple bias-correction on norms?

maya: Multiplied vectors by 1.06 -> recall@10 up to 0.800. Still ~0.014 down vs baseline.

eval-bot: eval-bot: UMAP & per-topic diffs uploaded: s3://redwood-dev-artifacts/6553210000/umap.tar.gz

reina: Run per-channel quant + small output offset correction. Also test asymmetric rounding vs symmetric; sometimes helps for token-like symbols.

maya: Kicked off per-channel + asymmetric rounding sweep (+/- scaling, bias) and a 5-bit ablation to test quality knee.

tom: Add a short-query routing rule for canary: queries <=3 tokens -> route to lumen-v1 during canary. Keeps user experience safe.

maya: Will add routing and attach sample IDs for top-100 failures. Repro script:
```bash
./run_holdout_eval.sh --model lumenix-int6 --holdout stack_holdout_8k \
  --k 10,100 --resamples 800 --slices short_queries,code_symbols --save-samples
```

reina: Thanks. If per-channel + offset closes >75% of gap and latency impact <3% we can consider canaryed rollout.

maya: Agreed. Posting sweep outputs in ~90m.
